topic: Ötzi the Iceman's 5,300-year-old backpack frame, older than the pyramids
title: The Oldest Backpack Ever Found Predates The Great Pyramid By 700 Years
description: AI-narrated commentary. In 1991, hikers found a 5,300-year-old frozen body in the Alps still carrying a wood-frame backpack, the oldest one ever discovered, decades before archaeologists realized its owner had been murdered.

hook_candidates.text: The oldest backpack ever found predates the Great Pyramid of Giza by 700 years.
The backpack isn't a modern invention. The oldest one on record is over 5,300 years old.
In 1991, two hikers in the Alps found a frozen body still strapped into its backpack.
What's the oldest backpack ever found, and why did its owner never make it home?

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who thinks backpacks are a recent invention, because they want to watch that assumption fall apart on the spot.
contradicted_belief: Most people think the backpack is basically a modern invention, but the oldest backpack ever found is thousands of years old.
closing_comment: The oldest backpack ever found is still shaping hiking gear design 5,300 years later, same frame and same idea, just older than the pyramids.

sources.note: Confirms Ötzi's pack was a U-shaped hazel rod frame with larch boards and a hide sack, carbon-dated ~3300 BCE.
Confirms a flint arrowhead lodged in Ötzi's shoulder tore his artery, the likely cause of death.
